hooks.name: Documentation Sync
hooks.description: Identifies documentation that needs updates when source files are saved

action.prompt:
📚 Documentation Sync Check

A source file was saved. Check if project documentation needs updates:

## 1. API Changes → Update OpenAPI Spec / API.md
   [ ] New endpoints added?
       - Add to `openapi.yaml` or `api-docs.json`
       - Include: path, method (GET/POST), request schema, response schema
   [ ] Endpoint parameters changed?
       - Update query params, path params, request body schema
       - Document new/removed fields
   [ ] Response schema changed?
       - Update response model in spec
       - Document new fields, types, status codes
   [ ] Error responses changed?
       - Update error schema (400, 404, 500, etc.)
       - Document new error codes or messages
   [ ] Authentication/authorization changed?
       - Update security requirements in spec
       - Document required scopes or roles

   📄 Files to check/update:
   - `openapi.yaml` or `swagger.json` (OpenAPI spec)
   - `docs/API.md` or `README.md` (human-readable API docs)
   - `src/routes/` or `src/api/` (route docstrings)

## 2. Function/Class Signature Changes → Update ARCHITECTURE.md & Docstrings
   [ ] New public functions or classes?
       - Add module description
       - Document parameters and return types
       - Document exceptions/error cases
   [ ] Function parameters changed?
       - Update docstring parameters
       - Mark parameters as deprecated if applicable
   [ ] Return type changed?
       - Update docstring @returns section
   [ ] Class properties or methods added/removed?
       - Update class diagram or interface documentation

   📄 Files to check/update:
   - `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (system design, class diagrams)
   - Inline docstrings in source files
   - Type definitions in `.d.ts` or type stubs

## 3. Configuration Changes → Update README.md Setup Section
   [ ] New environment variables required?
       - Add to `.env.example`
       - Document in README.md "Configuration" section
       - Note: NEVER commit actual .env with secrets
   [ ] Build/runtime dependencies added?
       - Add to README installation instructions
       - Note Python version, Node version requirements
   [ ] Database schema changed?
       - Update database setup instructions
       - Document migration commands
   [ ] New CLI commands or scripts added?
       - Add to README "Commands" or "Getting Started" section

   📄 Files to check/update:
   - `README.md` (installation, configuration)
   - `.env.example` (environment variables template)
   - `docs/SETUP.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md` (detailed setup)

## 4. Dependencies & Breaking Changes → Update CHANGELOG.md
   [ ] New dependencies added?
       - Document in CHANGELOG under "Added" section
       - Note version and purpose
   [ ] Dependencies updated?
       - Document major version bumps in CHANGELOG
       - Note if breaking changes affect users
   [ ] Breaking API changes?
       - Document migration path in CHANGELOG
       - Provide before/after examples
   [ ] Deprecated features?
       - Document deprecation timeline in CHANGELOG
       - Suggest replacement API

   📄 Files to check/update:
   - `CHANGELOG.md` (version history, breaking changes)
   - `package.json` / `pyproject.toml` (dependencies listed)
   - `docs/MIGRATION.md` (migration guides for major changes)

## 5. Type Definitions & Interfaces → Update Type Stubs
   [ ] New types or interfaces created?
       - Export from index.d.ts or types file
       - Document complex types with JSDoc
   [ ] Enum values changed?
       - Ensure type definitions match implementation
   [ ] Generic type parameters changed?
       - Update type stubs and documentation

   📄 Files to check/update:
   - `src/types.ts` or `src/types/index.ts`
   - `.d.ts` type definition files
   - TSDoc/JSDoc comments

## 6. Decision: Create Follow-Up or Include Updates

   **Option A: Include updates in current work**
   - If minimal changes needed (e.g., docstring fix)
   - Update docs now, commit alongside source changes
   - Mark as complete in this task

   **Option B: Create separate documentation task**
   - If extensive updates needed (e.g., new API endpoints with full OpenAPI redesign)
   - Create task: "Update API docs for feature X"
   - Link in this task's notes
   - Do NOT commit source without linked documentation task

## 7. Documentation Checklist
   [ ] Identified all documentation needing updates
   [ ] Updated or created follow-up task for each doc type
   [ ] Inline docstrings/comments added to code
   [ ] Example usage documented (if applicable)
   [ ] No broken links in docs
   [ ] New docs follow project style (markdown formatting, headings, code blocks)

⚠️  Do NOT mark source file as complete until documentation is either:
   1. Updated in this task, or
   2. Assigned to a separate, linked documentation task

Keeping docs in sync with code prevents user confusion and reduces onboarding friction.
